newsitem.title: USA: Unocal unit sets tender for $700 mln debt.
newsitem.headline: Unocal unit sets tender for $700 mln debt.

text.p: Unocal Corp on Thursday said its Union Oil Company of California unit has set an offer to purchase outstanding debt issues totaling $700 million.

The tender offer, commenced on Thursday, will expire 1700 EDT on May 22, 1997, unless extended, Unocal said. Salomon Brothers Inc, Goldman, Sachs & Co, Lehman Brothers and Morgan Stanley & Co Inc are dealer managers for the offer.
Securities covered are the 9-3/4 percent notes due December 1, 2000; 8-3/4 percent notes due August 15, 2001; and the 9-1/4 percent debentures due February 1, 2003.

The purchase price for each note will result from a yield to maturity equal to a fixed spread over the yield of a reference U.S. Treasury security at the time of tender. Those spreads are: plus 15 basis points for debt due 2000; plus 18 basis points for debt due 2001; and plus 22 basis points for debt due 2003.
The tender will paydown a portion of the $2.814 billion in Unocal debt outstanding as of April 30, 1997, according to a Unocal spokesman.
Proceeds from a March 31, 1997, sale of Unocal's West Coast refining, marketing and transportation assets, and cash from an earlier asset sale, will finance the offer.
